assertion_analysis.fails_if: Unconditional future-turn increments at promotion_requests.py:561 swap runnable A/B order in either inactive-phase case; the literal expected sequence fails.
Dropping or misclassifying RUNNING rows makes the running count differ from the independently specified phase fixture.
Dropping or misclassifying WAITING rows makes the parked count differ from the independently specified phase fixture.
Filtering inactive rows out of _pending_requests entirely fails membership; the ID is fixture identity, and the output can omit it, so this assertion is not a tautology.
Restoring unconditional turn increments selects younger B rather than the literal older A through the real tick; owner and review-wait stubs model unavailable inactive work.
Ignoring or over-expiring the ten-minute A completion makes older A win rather than literal B/A.
Forwarding a 60-second report window into scheduling ignores A history and makes report order differ from independently anchored drain order at line 178.
Counting history outside the report-rate window yields one at 60 seconds; ignoring valid history yields zero at 3600/7200 seconds.
A tick that selects a different first request than the independently anchored B/A sequence fails; drain_order is constrained at line 178 rather than supplied as tick input.

assertion_independence: No input-echo tautology found; output-to-output parity at lines 181 and 186 is anchored to the literal independent expected order at line 178; fixture identity membership at line 139 can fail if the result drops that row.
